0g:2025-12-11:0g-reward-contract-leaked-.name: 0G reward contract leaked-key emergencyWithdraw
0g:2025-12-11:0g-reward-contract-leaked-.reason: The 0G Foundation's statement (https://x.com/0G_Foundation/status/1999781517283737670), reported by ChainCatcher (https://www.chaincatcher.com/en/article/2229218), says AliCloud instances compromised through Next.js CVE-2025-66478 exposed a plaintext private key used for reward updates, and the attacker used it to call the alignment reward contract's privileged emergencyWithdraw, taking 520,010 0G plus 9.93 ETH and 4,200 USDT. The privileged function executed as designed for the key holder.

abstract:2025-02-18:cardex-exposed-sessi.name: Cardex exposed session-signer key drain
abstract:2025-02-18:cardex-exposed-sessi.reason: Abstract's post-mortem covered by The Block (https://www.theblock.co/post/341694/cardex-exploit-compromised-400000-worth-of-ether-across-9000-wallets-abstract) and Decrypt (https://decrypt.co/306608/cardex-game-exploit-drains-abstract-wallets) states that the Cardex game shipped the private key of its session signer in its website frontend; the attacker used it to execute transactions under the month-long session keys about 9,000 Abstract Global Wallets had granted Cardex, draining about 400k USD of ETH. The wallets correctly honored a validly delegated session key; the fault was key exposure in offchain code.

algorand:2023-02-27:myalgo-wallet-cdn-co.name: MyAlgo wallet CDN compromise
algorand:2023-02-27:myalgo-wallet-cdn-co.reason: DefiLlama records MyAlgo on Algorand, 9.2m USD, classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'CDN Compromise', targetType 'Wallet', language JavaScript. Algorand is not an eip155 chain, and the defective artefact was the wallet's browser JavaScript, served from a compromised CDN, which exfiltrated users' mnemonics; the subsequent transfers were valid Algorand payments signed with the stolen seeds. Both grounds bite independently: there is no EVM chain involved and no deployed contract executed any defective code, only client-side script outside any chain's state.

arbitrum:2023-02-20:hope-finance-trading.name: Hope Finance TradingHelper swap exit scam
arbitrum:2023-02-20:hope-finance-trading.reason: CertiK's findings reported by Cointelegraph (https://cointelegraph.com/news/hope-finance-exploit-results-in-2m-stolen-from-users-funds) show that on launch day the project's privileged address swapped the TradingHelper contract used by GenesisRewardPool for one routing funds to the scammer and staged a fake router, so the next OpenTrade call moved the genesis-pool deposits out; about 1,095 ETH (about 1.86m USD) went to Tornado Cash. The loss came from an owner-authorized contract substitution, not a defect exercisable by an unprivileged caller.

arbitrum:2023-05-18:swaprum-add-backdoor.name: Swaprum add() backdoor LP theft
arbitrum:2023-05-18:swaprum-add-backdoor.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-swaprum-rug-pull-may-2023) and CertiK's findings reported by Cointelegraph (https://cointelegraph.com/news/alleged-swaprum-rug-pull-swipes-three-million-in-customer-funds) show the Swaprum deployer upgraded the staking contracts after the audit to add a backdoor add() function, used it to take users' staked LP tokens, removed the liquidity and bridged about 1,628 ETH (about 2.95m USD) to Tornado Cash. The failing code was an owner-installed backdoor.

arbitrum:2024-01-22:concentric-vault-dep.name: Concentric vault deployer-key malicious upgrade
arbitrum:2024-01-22:concentric-vault-dep.reason: Neptune Mutual's analysis (https://neptunemutual.com/blog/how-was-concentric-finance-exploited/) and crypto.news (https://crypto.news/concentric-app-suffers-1-7m-social-engineering-hack-on-arbitrum/) show a team member was socially engineered into installing malware, the Concentric deployer key was stolen, and the attacker used its upgrade authority to replace the vault code, call adminMint for CONE LP tokens and burn them to withdraw pool assets, about 715.7 ETH (about 1.72m USD). Upgrade and admin-mint authority executed as designed for the stolen key.

arbitrum:2024-10-18:tapioca-dao-contribu.name: Tapioca DAO contributor-key vesting and USDO takeover
arbitrum:2024-10-18:tapioca-dao-contribu.reason: Tapioca's post-mortem (https://mirror.xyz/tapiocada0.eth/RVcRuKmJAavD05ObYsyYOHLDJ4gkEZKwyY_Y0Gx6gNc) and Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-tapioca-dao-hack-october-2024) show a DPRK 'contagious interview' implant stole a core contributor's keys; the attacker used them to take ownership of the TAP vesting contract and claim 30m TAP, and of the USDO contract to add a minter, mint USDO and drain the USDO/USDC pool, taking about 605 ETH and 3.1m USDC (about 4.65m USD). Ownership-gated functions behaved as designed.

arbitrum:2024-10-30:sunray-finance-key-c.name: Sunray Finance key-compromise SUN mint
arbitrum:2024-10-30:sunray-finance-key-c.reason: Cointelegraph (https://cointelegraph.com/news/btc-scammers-sunray-finance-crypto-sec) reports that on 2024-10-30 an attacker with a compromised Sunray key upgraded the protocol's contract, minted about 200 sextillion SUN (and took control of ARC) and dumped them into DEX pairs, cashing out about 2.1m USD in USDT of a 2.7-2.86m USD total; Sunray itself described 'a sudden issuance of Sunray treasury asset tokens'. The upgrade and mint went through the key holder's authority.

arbitrum:2025-01-08:orange-finance-singl.name: Orange Finance single-signer admin key takeover
arbitrum:2025-01-08:orange-finance-singl.reason: The lead's 2024-01-23 date does not match the only reported Orange Finance incident, dated 2025-01-08 by Rekt (https://rekt.news/orange-finance-rekt) and Web3 Is Going Great (https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/single/orange-finance-hack), for about 840k USD. There the admin multisig required a single signature, a leaked key let the attacker upgrade Orange's vault contracts and transfer their assets and approved user tokens, swapped through Uniswap, PancakeSwap and SushiSwap. The upgrade authority behaved as designed for the key holder.

arbitrum:2026-07-15:cascade-cls-vault-ca.name: Cascade CLS vault (Cascade Orbit L3, chain 27182)
arbitrum:2026-07-15:cascade-cls-vault-ca.reason: The CLS vault ran on Cascade's Arbitrum Orbit L3 (rollup 0x869E22EC4a03BF7145074396F1Cfa1385B1a61f2 on 42161, chainId()=27182), which has no public RPC or explorer, so the exploit transaction, vulnerable artifact and code age cannot be identified. Only settlement is observable on Arbitrum: L3 account 0xaab4ae284ee49f541edca49972d119b4e7e1b61c (EIP-7702, funded by EOA 0x285996ba0b464f841d3a63e88c7cc319d70d9b55) deposited 500+50 USDC via 0x444e4d6948e95a3c98b9b498262fb2b7a05fd544 (Arbitrum blocks 484235340, 484244315); Outbox.executeTransaction in 0xcd801d24eb5957a4b2739cd9c3b24ddfc470935479d747e2b418a9a752578314 (block 484256243, index 1; L3 block 708106) paid 1,343,921.816016 USDC from L1USDCGateway proxy 0x6b01ca28 to the EOA (WithdrawalFinalized exitNum 0xb10; gateway USDC 2,585,633.586709 -> 1,241,711.770693), and 8,999 USDC followed in 0x36bd74193ecb69e8fc1e1d31537516681380d6b7f4ad5f9397b68b5abe237263. These are canonical bridge payouts of L3 balances, not execution of the vulnerable code. Reported mechanisms conflict (contract flaw; oracle/spot manipulation; mark-price and liquidation manipulation) and an offchain matching engine cannot be excluded. Reopen if a chain-27182 RPC or archive becomes available.

arbitrum:2026-07-22:afx-bridge-validator.name: AFX Bridge validator key compromise
arbitrum:2026-07-22:afx-bridge-validator.reason: DefiLlama classifies the $24.15m loss as validator key compromise; the bridge honored signatures from compromised validator keys.

base:2024-03-21:ticker-airdrop-developer.name: TICKER airdrop-developer token dump
base:2024-03-21:ticker-airdrop-developer.reason: DailyCoin (https://dailycoin.com/ticker-presale-ends-in-900k-theft-by-french-developer/) and CoinEdition (https://coinedition.com/crypto-sleuth-identifies-french-devs-massive-ticker-theft-of-900k/), citing ZachXBT, report that after an 877 ETH presale the TICKER team sent 15% of supply to the developer hired to run the airdrop, who instead sold 13% of supply for about 900k USD on Base and bridged the ETH out via Orbiter Finance. A trusted insider sold tokens he had been given; no deployed code failed.

base:2024-04-15:grand-base-deployer-key-.name: Grand Base deployer-key GB mint
base:2024-04-15:grand-base-deployer-key-.reason: Neptune Mutual (https://medium.com/neptune-mutual/understanding-the-grand-base-exploit-82a1ead971dc) and Cointelegraph (https://cointelegraph.com/news/base-asset-tokenization-protocol-compromised) show a developer's PC was hacked, exposing the deployer/LP wallet that held the GB token's mint authority and liquidity; the attacker minted and sold about 32.5m GB against a 50m cap and pulled liquidity for about 808.57 ETH (about 2m USD) around 03:00 UTC on 2024-04-15. The mint executed through the owner's authority as designed. The lead's 2024-04-09 date predates the reported incident.

base:2024-07-20:ethtrustfund-treasury-ex.name: ETHTrustFund treasury exit
base:2024-07-20:ethtrustfund-treasury-ex.reason: Cointelegraph (https://cointelegraph.com/news/ethtrustfund-dao-transfers-treasury-apparent-rug-pull) and crypto.news (https://crypto.news/ethtrustfund-rug-pulls-on-base-leading-to-2m-in-investor-losses/) report that on 2024-07-20 the developers of the Olympus fork moved about 607 ETH (about 2.1m USD) from the treasury they controlled to Ethereum, then through Tornado Cash and Railgun, and deleted all websites and social accounts. The team withdrew treasury funds under its own authority.

base:2025-11-21:aerodrome-and-velodrome-.name: Aerodrome and Velodrome registrar DNS hijack
base:2025-11-21:aerodrome-and-velodrome-.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-aerodrome-finance-hack-november-2025) and The Block (https://www.theblock.co/post/380037/top-dexs-aerodrome-velodrome-hit-with-front-end-compromise-urge-users-to-avoid-main-domains) report that DNS records for the protocols' centralized domains were altered, traced to an insider at registrar NameSilo, to serve a malicious copy of the frontend that phished approvals, costing users about 700k USD; the Aerodrome and Velodrome contracts were not compromised.

base:2025-11-24:basisos-agentic-fof-insi.name: BasisOS Agentic FoF insider vault theft
base:2025-11-24:basisos-agentic-fof-insi.reason: BasisOS' disclosure reported by Bitget News (https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560605078975) and Nominis' November report (https://www.nominis.io/insights/nominis-monthly-report-crypto-attacks-in-november-2025) says an internal engineer who ran the agent wrapper code had manually controlled the Agentic Fund of Funds vault behind the purported AI agent since launch and stole about 531k USD. An operator key holder withdrew funds he controlled.

base:2026-04-29:syndicate-commons-bridge.name: Syndicate Commons bridge upgrade-key leak
base:2026-04-29:syndicate-commons-bridge.reason: Syndicate Labs' statement reported by crypto.news (https://crypto.news/syndicate-labs-suffers-380k-synd-bridge-exploit-pledges-full-user-compensation/) and Coincu (https://coincu.com/syndicate-private-key-leak-malicious-bridge-contract-upgrade-380k-loss/) says the single upgrade key of the Commons bridge, stored unencrypted in a password manager, leaked and was used to install a malicious implementation, draining about 18.5m SYND and user funds (about 380k USD). The upgrade authority behaved as designed for the key holder.

base:2026-05-19:bankr-ai-agent-wallet-pr.name: Bankr AI agent wallet prompt-injection drains
base:2026-05-19:bankr-ai-agent-wallet-pr.reason: AMBCrypto (https://ambcrypto.com/ai-linked-wallet-drained-via-prompt-injection-in-bankr-exploit/) and CoinTurk (https://en.coin-turk.com/bankr-halts-swaps-after-440000-ai-exploit-hits-users/) report that attackers used prompt injection and social engineering against Bankr's AI agent, which controls custodial user wallets, to have it transfer funds out of 14 wallets, about 440k USD in linked addresses, after which Bankr paused swaps and transfers. The transfers were validly signed by the agent's own keys on instruction from its offchain model; no contract failed.

bitcoin:2024-04-29:rain-exchange-custodi.name: Rain exchange custodial wallet drain
bitcoin:2024-04-29:rain-exchange-custodi.reason: About 14.8m USD was taken from the custodial wallets of Rain, the Bahrain-licensed exchange, across Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and Solana on 2024-04-29; DefiLlama classifies the event as a private-key compromise and the public reporting attributes it to DPRK-linked actors, with no protocol or contract exploit alleged by any source. Three of the four asset legs are on non-eip155 chains and all four are exchange custody addresses, i.e. externally owned accounts moved with stolen keys, so there is no victim contract, no exploit transaction against deployed code and nothing whose code age could be measured. SlowMist Hacked carries no entry for this incident and I could not obtain a spot-checkable address for any leg; the exclusion ground does not depend on one.

bitcoin:2024-05-31:dmm-bitcoin-custody-t.name: DMM Bitcoin custody theft
bitcoin:2024-05-31:dmm-bitcoin-custody-t.reason: The stolen asset was 4,502.9 BTC out of DMM Bitcoin's Bitcoin hot wallet (theft transaction 975ec405ac9dc9fa5ab8009d94d6a1fe31dff8a8127ea90d023104e52754e4d7, consolidation address 1B6rJRfjTXwEy36SCs5zofGMmdv2kdZw7P, then ten 500-BTC splits). Bitcoin is not an eip155 chain and no EVM contract held, released or accounted for the funds, so no executed EVM code exists to age. The joint FBI, DC3 and Japan NPA advisory of 2024-12-23 attributes the loss to DPRK TraderTraitor operators who social-engineered an employee of Ginco, DMM's wallet-management software vendor, with a fake pre-employment coding test, then used stolen session cookies to impersonate that employee inside Ginco's unencrypted communications system and alter a legitimate DMM withdrawal request in late May 2024. That is an offchain infrastructure and credential failure. EVM chains appear only downstream, when proceeds were bridged through THORChain to Ethereum and Avalanche during laundering, which is not victim depletion.

bitcoin:2025-09-24:sbi-crypto-mining-poo.name: SBI Crypto mining pool wallet drain
bitcoin:2025-09-24:sbi-crypto-mining-poo.reason: ZachXBT reported roughly 21m USD of suspicious outflows on 2025-09-24 from wallets belonging to SBI Group's mining subsidiary SBI Crypto, in BTC, ETH, LTC, DOGE and BCH, routed through five instant-exchange services and then into Tornado Cash, with suspected DPRK involvement; CoinDesk carried the report and SlowMist Hacked records it. Four of the five asset legs are on non-eip155 chains and every leg is a custodial mining-pool wallet, i.e. an externally owned account, so no deployed contract executed and no protocol invariant failed. I checked the only publicly labelled EVM address for the entity, Etherscan's 'SBI Crypto Pool' 0x8b4de256180cfec54c436a470af50f9ee2813dbb, and it has no transactions at all in blocks 23422005-23443482 (2025-09-23 to 2025-09-26), so that label is not the drained wallet and no EVM victim contract can be named.

bitcoin:2026-05-01:bisq-v1-negative-mine.name: Bisq v1 negative miner-fee trade protocol exploit
bitcoin:2026-05-01:bisq-v1-negative-mine.reason: Bisq's post-mortem (https://bisq.network/blog/security-incident-post-mortem/) states that a modified client exploited missing validation of the taker-defined miner fee, which could be negative, to manipulate the Bitcoin multisig trade output and take about 11.6 BTC (about 876k USD) from ten users' offers. Bisq is an offchain Java trade protocol settling on Bitcoin; no eip155 code is involved.

bitcoin:2026-07-15:teleswap-bitcoin-hot-.name: TeleSwap Bitcoin hot wallet outflows
bitcoin:2026-07-15:teleswap-bitcoin-hot-.reason: Bitget News (https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560605520572) and Protos (https://protos.com/across-allbridge-teleswap-lost-5-7m-to-bridge-hacks-in-past-week/), citing ZachXBT, report suspicious outflows of more than 735k USD from TeleSwap's Bitcoin hot wallet on 2026-07-15, after which the wallet stopped processing and funds went to Tornado Cash; the team gave no contract-level explanation. The drained wallet is a Bitcoin address, so no eip155 victim code is implicated.

bittensor:2024-07-02:bittensor-malicious.name: Bittensor malicious PyPI package coldkey exfiltration
bittensor:2024-07-02:bittensor-malicious.reason: A malicious release of the `bittensor` Python package on PyPI exfiltrated users' unencrypted coldkeys, and the attacker then signed ordinary balance transfers on the Bittensor (Subtensor) Substrate chain. DefiLlama records language 'Python', classification 'Social Engineering', technique 'Malware', 8,000,000 USD, dated 2024-07-02, with an empty chain list. Bittensor is an SS58 Substrate network with no eip155 chain id and no EVM contract state at the time of the incident, and the defect lives in an off-chain Python dependency. Both cohort condition 1 (executed EVM code) and condition 2 (an eip155 anchor) fail.

blast:2024-02-25:riskonblast-team-exit-w.name: RiskOnBlast team exit with presale ETH
blast:2024-02-25:riskonblast-team-exit-w.reason: CoinDesk (https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2024/02/26/blast-ecosystem-sees-first-apparent-scam-as-riskonblast-rug-pulls-13m-ether) and Web3 Is Going Great (https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/?id=riskonblast-gambling-platform-rug-pulls-for-1-3-million) report that the anonymous RiskOnBlast team took the more than 420 ETH (about 1.3m USD) raised from over 750 wallets and sent it to ChangeNOW, MEXC and Bybit before disappearing. The team controlled the funds; no exploit of deployed code by an outside caller occurred.

blast:2024-07-24:monoswap-developer-info.name: MonoSwap developer infostealer key compromise
blast:2024-07-24:monoswap-developer-info.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-monoswap-hack-july-2024) and SlowMist (https://slowmist.medium.com/cunning-phishing-in-the-dark-forest-493221c34687) show attackers posing as VCs got a MonoSwap developer to install a fake 'Kakao' meeting app that was an infostealer; with the developer's keys, which held full control of the project's wallets and contracts, they took over the staking contracts and withdrew users' staked liquidity, at least 1.3m USD. The contracts honored their owner's stolen keys.

bouncebit:2026-08-19:bouncebit-chain-lev.name: BounceBit chain-level unauthorized transfers
bouncebit:2026-08-19:bouncebit-chain-lev.reason: DefiLlama records BounceBit as classification 'Access Control', targetType 'Chain', language 'Go', $3.0m. SlowMist's entry (2026-08-19, citing x.com/bouncebit/article/2090785561800061430) says an attacker exploited a protocol-level authorization flaw in the Evmos stack to move about 286.5M native BB from nine mainnet accounts in 14 transactions, with no keys or signatures compromised. BounceBit then sunset the L1 and reissued BB on BNB Chain from a pre-attack snapshot. The defect is in the chain's Go node/Cosmos-SDK modules, not in deployed EVM contract code. The 14 transactions were not enumerated onchain (no BounceBit RPC configured).

bsc:2021-09-19:pnetwork-pbtc-bridge-forg.name: pNetwork pBTC bridge forged-event drain (September 2021)
bsc:2021-09-19:pnetwork-pbtc-bridge-forg.reason: The loss was 277 BTC, about 12.7m USD, released from pNetwork's Bitcoin-side vault. DefiLlama records the event as 'Bridge & Cross-Chain' / 'Spoofed Event Log' over chains BSC and Bitcoin, and names the defective code's language as Rust: the pTokens bridge core that decides whether a redeem happened is Rust software running off-chain, not EVM bytecode. I verified onchain that the BSC side lost nothing. The pBTC token 0xed28a457a5a76596ac48d87c0f577020f6ea1c4c (AdminUpgradeabilityProxy over implementation 0xd61372d1c3e0a0925467317425359fb2959fe186) has zero Transfer events from the zero address in blocks 11035530 (2021-09-18T23:59:58Z) through 11092771 (2021-09-21), i.e. no unbacked mint, and the largest single pBTC movement in that whole window is 51.7499 pBTC at block 11067993 (tx 0x2876012ade42384bd6a5abe3326f4fa1c02b13c7121e8333b49216b8d9e3e88e), nowhere near 277. So there is no EVM victim contract: the depleted asset is native BTC on a non-eip155 chain and the failure is an off-chain validator honouring a log it did not authenticate, the same shape as the already-excluded THORChain Bifrost incidents.

bsc:2022-10-11:qanx-bridge-profanity-der.name: QANX bridge Profanity-derived deployer key compromise
bsc:2022-10-11:qanx-bridge-profanity-der.reason: Numen Cyber's analysis (https://medium.com/numen-cyber-labs/the-private-key-of-qanplatform-was-cracked-by-hackers-causing-1-9-million-losses-8673a54fbb20) shows the QANX bridge deployer 0x68e8198d5b3b3639372358542b92eb997c5c314a was a vanity address generated with a Profanity-derived tool whose private key was recoverable; the attacker used that key's bridge authority to withdraw about 1.44bn QANX on BNB Chain and 1.43bn QANX on Ethereum, selling for about 3,090 BNB and 255 ETH (about 1.16m USD cashed out). The bridge access control executed as designed for the key holder; the fault is key generation, not deployed code.

bsc:2022-12-26:bitkeep-trojanised-androi.name: BitKeep trojanised Android APK distribution
bsc:2022-12-26:bitkeep-trojanised-androi.reason: Attackers repackaged BitKeep's Android wallet (v7.2.9) with code that exfiltrated users' private keys and distributed it through unofficial download mirrors; the resulting drains are ordinary ERC-20/BEP-20 transfer and native-value transactions signed out of the victims' own externally owned accounts on BNB Chain, Ethereum, Polygon and Tron. The compromised artefact is a Java/Kotlin APK, not deployed EVM bytecode, and no contract in the causal path failed any invariant - the token contracts executed correctly for a caller holding the keys. There is therefore no victim contract and no defect-bearing code state to age. Compromised credentials and off-chain client behaviour are both excluded by METHODOLOGY.

bsc:2023-06-10:atlantis-loans-abandoned-.name: Atlantis Loans abandoned GovernorBravo takeover
bsc:2023-06-10:atlantis-loans-abandoned-.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-atlantis-loans-hack-june-2023) and Neptune Mutual (https://medium.com/neptune-mutual/understanding-atlantis-loans-exploit-3716f7e765b4) show that after the team abandoned the protocol, the attacker passed a GovernorBravo proposal created on 2023-06-07 (an April attempt, proposal 49, had missed quorum) that after the 172,800-second timelock made an attacker contract admin of the ABep20Delegator proxies, then pointed them at a backdoored implementation and used users' lingering approvals to pull about 2.5m USD. Governance executed a validly passed vote; acquiring and voting governance power is not a defect in executed EVM code.

bsc:2023-07-27:defilabs-vpoolv6-withdraw.name: DefiLabs vPoolv6 withdrawFunds backdoor
bsc:2023-07-27:defilabs-vpoolv6-withdraw.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-defi-labs-rug-pull-july-2023) and Web3 Is Going Great (https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/?id=defilabs-rug-pull) show that after announcing maintenance, the privileged address 0xee08... called the owner-only withdrawFunds() in DefiLabs' vPoolv6 contract and removed about 1.4m BSC-USD (about 1.6m USD in total). The function worked as its authors intended for the project's own key; no unprivileged defect is involved.

bsc:2024-03-22:lucky-star-currency-post-.name: Lucky Star Currency post-rug ownership drain
bsc:2024-03-22:lucky-star-currency-post-.reason: Blockfence's March 2024 report (https://blockfence.io/security/web3-security-incidents-report-march-2024-blockfence/) classifies it as a rug pull: on 2024-03-22 ownership of the Lucky Star Currency project, already exposed by CertiK as a 1.1m USD exit scam in October 2023 (https://www.certik.com/resources/blog/lucky-star-currency-exit-scam), was transferred to a malicious contract that drained almost 300k USD of tokens from remaining holders. The drain ran through owner authority transferred by the project's own key.

bsc:2024-07-15:rehold-co-founder-unautho.name: ReHold co-founder unauthorized withdrawal
bsc:2024-07-15:rehold-co-founder-unautho.reason: ReHold CTO Michael Semin's disclosure (https://medium.com/@bifotofficial/700-000-unauthorized-withdrawal-from-rehold-protocol-full-disclosure-and-next-steps-097119d545cd) and the Quadriga Initiative case (https://www.quadrigainitiative.com/hackfraudscam/reholdrenatgafarovsmartcontractwithdrawal.php) state that on 2024-07-15 co-founder Renat Gafarov used his own privileged access to withdraw more than 700k USD of protocol profits and founders' capital from ReHold's contracts without his partner's approval, disclosed on 2024-09-26. A key holder withdrew through the owner path as designed.

bsc:2025-09-23:seedify-sfund-bridge-deve.name: Seedify SFUND bridge developer-key mint
bsc:2025-09-23:seedify-sfund-bridge-deve.reason: Seedify's disclosure reported by Cryptonews (https://cryptonews.com/news/sfund-token-crashes-99-as-north-korean-hackers-drain-1-2m-from-seedify-bridge/) and Brave New Coin (https://bravenewcoin.com/insights/sfund-token-crashes-99-as-north-korean-hackers-drain-1-2m-from-seedify-bridge) says a DPRK-linked group obtained a Seedify developer's private keys around 12:05 UTC on 2025-09-23 and used their bridge authority to mint SFUND across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base and BNB Chain, dumping it for about 1.2-1.7m USD. The mint went through the developer key's privileges.

bsc:2025-09-24:griffin-ai-gain-admin-eoa.name: Griffin AI GAIN admin-EOA OFT peer swap
bsc:2025-09-24:griffin-ai-gain-admin-eoa.reason: QuillAudits (https://www.quillaudits.com/blog/hack-analysis/griffin-ai-exploit) and BeInCrypto (https://beincrypto.com/griffin-ai-gain-token-crash-exploit/) show the attacker controlled GAIN's admin EOA and used setPeer to replace the official Ethereum OFT peer 0xccdbb9... with an attacker contract 0x7a8caf..., then sent LayerZero messages from it to mint 5bn GAIN on BNB Chain and sold 147.5m for 2,955 BNB (about 3m USD). The OFT correctly trusted the peer its owner configured; the malicious peer was attack machinery, not a latent vulnerability.

bsc:2025-11-20:gana-payment-ownership-ta.name: GANA Payment ownership takeover reward drain
bsc:2025-11-20:gana-payment-ownership-ta.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-gana-payment-hack-november-2025) and Cryptonews, citing ZachXBT (https://cryptonews.com/news/zachxbt-reveals-bsc-project-gana-payment-hit-with-3-1m-exploit/), report that an attacker with the project's stolen owner key transferred contract ownership to himself, raised the reward rate, and used unstake to collect inflated GANA rewards, laundering about 1,140 BNB and 346.8 ETH (about 3.1m USD) through Tornado Cash. Owner-only parameter changes behaved as designed.

bsc:2025-12-09:debot-custodial-wallet-ke.name: DeBot custodial wallet key theft
bsc:2025-12-09:debot-custodial-wallet-ke.reason: SlowMist's alert and DeBot's statement reported by Bitget News (https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560605124233, https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560605124368) say an intrusion from a Japanese data center detected on 2025-12-09 exposed private keys of DeBot trading-bot wallets created before 2025-12-10; the attacker drained about 255k USD from those wallets, consolidating on BNB Chain and routing through Tornado Cash, and DeBot compensated users. The victims are custodial EOAs emptied with stolen keys.

bsc:2026-02-25:holdstation-app-update-su.name: Holdstation app-update supply-chain injection
bsc:2026-02-25:holdstation-app-update-su.reason: Holdstation's disclosure reported by Bitget News (https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560605224859, https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560605218450) says the attacker stole a developer's session token, bypassed two-factor authentication and injected malicious code into a Holdstation smart-wallet application update (Worldchain and BNB Chain), which then stole about 462k USDT from users; Holdstation suspended services and promised compensation, and Verichains confirmed the contracts were secure. The loss originates in the distributed client software, not in deployed contract logic.

bsc:2026-05-27:superfortune-gua-airdrop-.name: SUPERFORTUNE GUA airdrop multisig destination tampering
bsc:2026-05-27:superfortune-gua-airdrop-.reason: SUPERFORTUNE's statement (https://x.com/SUPERFORTUNE888/status/2059818459421372485) and Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-superfortune-ai-hack-may-2026) say a multisig transaction meant to fund the airdrop claim contract 0x70ae7D3DECfB4C3aE996fb1c07092566F73D5c15 was signed and executed with the lookalike destination 0x70AE678b457C5E1b3fD7AD9537F234dFc1795C15, sending about 15m GUA to the attacker, who sold for about 5.66m USD; classic address poisoning was ruled out in favor of compromised tooling or workflow. bsc:2026-07-30:swan-treasury-zhaiquanbuy.name: Swan Treasury ZhaiquanBuy leaked signer key
bsc:2026-07-30:swan-treasury-zhaiquanbuy.reason: Crypto.news (https://crypto.news/swan-treasury-loses-625k-after-signer-key-leak-enables-discounted-sty-purchases/) and Nominis' July report (https://www.nominis.io/insights/nominis-monthly-report-crypto-exploits-and-attacks-in-july-2026) show the attacker held the private key of the offchain signer hardcoded as _signer in the ZhaiquanBuy contract and produced valid signatures with discount 1, buying about 687,000 STY at about 1/100 of price and selling it into the STY/USDT pool for about 625k USD. cardano:2026-06-21:secondfi-yoroi-predic.name: SecondFi (Yoroi) predictable-nonce key disclosure
cardano:2026-06-21:secondfi-yoroi-predic.reason: A public analysis of the SecondFi signer (https://hackmd.io/@QmCYMVNVQuqRJhiqMlXVdA/ry2LIyiMGx) and Crypto Briefing (https://cryptobriefing.com/secondfi-exploit-drains-cardano-users/) show the wallet's Ed25519 signing code produced predictable nonces, so private keys could be reconstructed from public Cardano signatures; about 16m ADA (about 2.4m USD) was taken from 374 addresses between 2026-06-21 and 06-23 and EMURGO wound the wallet down. The flaw is in client key handling on Cardano.

cardano:2026-07-21:wanchain-cardano-brid.name: Wanchain Cardano bridge signature verification flaw
cardano:2026-07-21:wanchain-cardano-brid.reason: DefiLlama records the incident on Cardano only, 10m USD, classification 'Input Validation', technique 'Signature Verification Flaw', bridgeHack true, targetType 'Chain', and names the defective code's language as Haskell. Wanchain's Cardano-side bridge logic is a Plutus validator written in Plutus Tx / Haskell and addressed by a Cardano script address, so there is neither an eip155 address nor EVM runtime bytecode whose age this dataset could measure, and the depleted vault is on Cardano rather than on the BNB Chain leg the web lead names. The cohort is eip155-only. Re-enter only if a postmortem shows the released value actually came out of a Wanchain contract deployed on BNB Chain or another eip155 chain, which would move the victim onto an EVM chain.

eip155:10:0x8761164b8947a0690b57896a8e73.name: Cozy Finance
eip155:10:0x8761164b8947a0690b57896a8e73.reason: The verified UMATrigger contracts 0xeb6613fac35fed17c276e3fe45d67da67685f1ef (market 5, 'Did Aave v2 get hacked?') and 0xacd105feea362d5c27caaba0b45f53d91b92de27 (market 0, 'Did Curve get hacked?') bind an immutable UMA OptimisticOracleV2 0x255483434aba5a75dc60c1391bb162bcd9de2882 (verified OptimisticOracleV2). priceProposed, priceSettled and priceDisputed accept only oracle callbacks for their own identifier, timestamp and query. runProgrammaticCheck calls oracle.settle only once oracle.hasPrice is true, and TRIGGERED is set only from the settled answer 1e18. TX1 0x53b454a3f552c5498994f74ae8737faa60123cac274bdd3b0383ccb226b3f2cb (block 156364035:54, 2026-09-02T05:27:27Z): attacker EOA 0x003fe7359a4e03c85ac2f521ec699ed84c7c5ccb, via 0x9e47c805587362ef36f2cab9d1e4e7d546f953d4, bought 96,596.967870 + 65,715.735793 USDC.e of protection on Set 0x17705474 while both markets were ACTIVE. It then proposed YES with 500 USDC.e bonds; two OO ProposePrice logs follow and both triggers froze. getLogs for ProposalDisputed on both triggers over blocks 156364035-156580507 returns 0, so the 432,000 s liveness passed with no dispute. TX2 0x8761164b (block 156580507:23) settled both requests and claimed. The Set paid 160,776.340904 USDC.e to the attack contract (Set USDC.e balance 162,312.703663 at block 156364034, 4,168.126922 at 156580507), and 163,326.3437 USDC.e went on to 0xeb2d41bcb3c3be8be5d74942fa2deb601448e240. Neither Aave v2 nor Curve suffered a loss of 50% or more after block 17187855, so the settled YES was false. It became final only through the external oracle's undisputed-liveness rule on abandoned markets. Buying protection before the proposal falls in the intended pre-freeze window, so no Cozy executed-code invariant was violated.

eip155:137:0x70f7e0376c25dcd0dd9263bdd3a.name: GAMEE GMEE deployer-key recoverERC721s drain
eip155:137:0x70f7e0376c25dcd0dd9263bdd3a.reason: Halborn's analysis and GAMEE's own disclosure attribute the loss to unauthorised access to an outdated GitLab repository that contained the project deployer's private key. Onchain, the compromised owner 0x566b788de3969d35711f6a0fc543b00ed7260cdc called the owner-only rescue function recoverERC721s (selector 0xc3666c36) on the verified PolygonGMEE token 0xcf32822ff397ef82425153a9dcb726e5ff61dca7 twice, at 2024-01-22T18:31:15Z (block 52629016, moving 299,999,999 GMEE to 0x16afa519642c932b073cd21d82162bdc7a471b86) and again at 20:31:03Z, then called transferOwnership on the same token at 22:35:32Z and on roughly fifteen further GAMEE contracts between 2024-01-23T03:10Z and 04:02Z. The PolygonGMEE source exposes recoverERC20s/recoverERC721s behind a _requireOwnership guard that executed exactly as written for the legitimate owner address, so no deployed-code invariant was violated; the defect is credential storage in an off-chain repository. Total press figure roughly 600m GMEE, about 7m USD.

eip155:137:0xbb1452e04d9b3451dd2f08920de.name: bZx Polygon and BSC deployer key compromise
eip155:137:0xbb1452e04d9b3451dd2f08920de.reason: The contracts' ownership checks all passed because the attacker held the owner key. The victims are the verified bZxProtocol 0xfe4f0eb0a1ad109185c9aade64c48ff8e928e54b (Polygon, created block 14612379, 2021-05-17T17:32:45Z) and LoanToken 0x97ebf27d40d306ad00bb2922e02c58264b295a95 (Polygon, block 14964301, 2021-05-26T20:49:03Z), plus bZxProtocol 0xc47812857a74425e2039b57891a3dfcf51602d5d on BNB Chain, all deployed by the bZx developer EOA 0xb7f72028d9b502dc871c444363a7ac5a52546608. Exactly one OwnershipTransferred event exists on each between deployment and the incident: Polygon bZxProtocol at block 21009330, 2021-11-05T11:07:16Z, anchor transaction 0xbb1452e04d9b3451dd2f08920deadf3009e1e8233289cd628a391bdc1c37555d, moving ownership from 0xb7f72028d9b502dc871c444363a7ac5a52546608 to the fresh EOA 0x0acc0e5faa09cb1976237c3a9af3d3d4b2f35fa5; the LoanToken follows at block 21009382 (0xc078907ec967b68f257b5d809ab71dbbc56288d158861de6b357ed0aea59fd75) and the BNB Chain protocol at block 12386620 (0x9b16f5e8a648f72be3f9657880b26e525018e40e8873a14161690f8f48bf01b9). owner() read at block 21009445 is 0x0acc0e5f..., and that same address then calls selector 0x55072d96 with the collector 0x74487eed1e67f4787e8c0570e8d5d168a05254d4 as argument to sweep 5.88210232 WBTC (block 21009446, 0x028d92aac9e58572d6099973729ebfbdfa405566a5aa2386cad6a0744876f107), then 568.54 WETH, 27.35 WBTC and 283,459.66 WMATIC at 11:15:02Z, and on BNB Chain 651.01 WBNB, 56,162.25 CAKE, 11.91 BTCB and 87.80 ETH at 11:14:07Z. bZx's post-mortem states that a developer opened a phishing email carrying a macro-bearing Word document which ran a script that stole his wallet mnemonic; that EOA controlled the Polygon and BSC deployments. Ethereum was unaffected because it was under DAO control. A compromised owner key is not a defect in executed code.

eip155:1:0x0b21a19d9b52fe001366e7d417acf.name: BtcTurk second custodial-wallet incident
eip155:1:0x0b21a19d9b52fe001366e7d417acf.reason: The drained wallets are externally owned accounts and the drain is a scripted sequence of signed transfers, not a contract exploit. eth_getCode returns 0x for 0xb5a46bc8b76fd2825aeb43db9c9e89e89158ecde, 0xde2faca4bbc0aca08ff04d387c39b6f6325bf82a and 0x2cea0297bfb1b55ff37126b677d78e2b1fd2e856. The anchor transaction at block 23138830 is a plain 345.95065004784965 ETH value transfer with empty calldata from 0xb5a46bc8b76fd2825aeb43db9c9e89e89158ecde to the attacker consolidation account 0x7d91d1ebeba91257733a523409125aedac5d8b6e, followed by ERC-20 transfers of FLOKI, PAXG, PEPE, ENA, AAVE, OM and LINK at roughly 12-second intervals across Ethereum, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Mantle and Polygon, plus non-eip155 Bitcoin and Solana legs. Rekt and Halborn both conclude leaked hot wallet private keys, the same failure mode as BtcTurk's June 2024 incident; BtcTurk published no post-mortem. Distinct from the 2024-06-22 BtcTurk row: different chains, different wallets and a different attacker cluster.

eip155:1:0x1abab4c8db9a30e703114528e31de.name: SmartMesh
eip155:1:0x1abab4c8db9a30e703114528e31de.reason: The selected transaction exploits transferProxy's unchecked _value + _feeSmt addition and creates artificial SMT ledger balances, but its receipt and call trace transfer no ETH or external reserve asset. eip155:1:0x1ae232da212c45f35c1525f851e4c.name: Kelp DAO rsETH OFTAdapter forged LayerZero packet
eip155:1:0x1ae232da212c45f35c1525f851e4c.reason: Kelp set the Ethereum receive route for source eid 30320 in transaction 0x2d48d9331d96c46f8b4a9f7a7bdcf256d2034dadb42f039d27dc28077d520592 to require DVN 0x589dedbd617e0cbcb916a9223f4d1300c294236b with 42 confirmations and no optional DVN. The setting persisted through the incident. In transaction 0xfe575668f895e10f8496fca3bb928fa53bebbea3e1de567d61bcd12d935f0d6f, that DVN's execute path accepted its own multisig authorization and called ReceiveUln302.verify for the forged nonce-308 packet. ReceiveUln302 then correctly counted the configured DVN, and permissionless commitVerification and lzReceive released 116,500 rsETH. A one-DVN route makes one verifier compromise sufficient, but it is the explicit trust model, not an EVM code or causal-configuration defect; the verifier authorized false offchain data while every onchain authorization check held.

eip155:1:0x26109c1fb2a71485f47176c6046fe.name: THORChain ETH Router forged Deposit log (second 2021 incident)
eip155:1:0x26109c1fb2a71485f47176c6046fe.reason: The loss came from THORChain Bifrost accepting a forged log, not from a defect in the deployed router. Six returnVaultAssets calls in block 12878653 (indices 38,40,42,44,46,48) pass router=0x0 and asgard=attacker contract, so the empty coins loop runs and the unconditional asgard.call{value: msg.value} executes attacker code; that contract then emits the router Deposit topic0 0xef519b7e.. from its own address with topic1 = Asgard vault 0xf56cba49.., carrying each vaults full vaultAllowance read by staticcall in the same block. Bifrost matched logs by topic without checking the emitter and the real Asgard vault then signed legitimate transferOut payouts memoed REFUND:<returnVaultAssets txhash>. The routers own invariants held: vaultAllowance was never mis-decremented and no router asset moved except through the vaults authorised transferOut. THORChains post-mortem locates both bugs and both fixes in Bifrost, and the router runtime 0x8adfb73731c56be8d5d0300c3007489df1f935a40de483e803ef509935950b91 is identical at blocks 12796668, 12828215, 12833113, 12878652 and 13700000, so no redeployment followed. Noted for any future widening of the cohort: returnVaultAssets has no access control and makes an arbitrary external call, which is what let attacker code run inside a router-addressed transaction; that was judged a bypassed precondition rather than an invariant failure of the executed code.

eos:2021-05-14:flash-sx-vaults-sx-eos-re.name: flash.sx / vaults.sx EOS reentrancy drain
eos:2021-05-14:flash-sx-vaults-sx-eos-re.reason: DefiLlama places the incident on EOS and records the defective code's language as C++. EOSIO contracts are C++ compiled to WASM and are addressed by 12-character account names, not by eip155 addresses, so there is no address, no runtime bytecode and no codeHash the verifier could resolve. The cohort is eip155-only, so it is excluded on chain grounds regardless. Re-enter only if the cohort is ever widened beyond eip155.

ethereum:2021-03-14:roll-social-money-ho.name: Roll social-money hot wallet key compromise
ethereum:2021-03-14:roll-social-money-ho.reason: Roll's statements reported by TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/2021/03/23/roll-still-doesnt-know-how-its-hot-wallet-was-hacked/) and Decrypt (https://decrypt.co/61349/a-5-7-million-crypto-heist-leaves-social-tokens-in-freefall) attribute the roughly 5.7m USD loss to compromise of the private key of Roll's custodial hot wallet, explicitly not a bug in its smart contracts or social-token contracts; the attacker moved the wallet's creator tokens by ordinary signed transfers, sold them on Uniswap for about 3,000 ETH and routed part through Tornado Cash. ethereum:2021-07-10:anyswap-v3-router-mp.name: Anyswap V3 router MPC key recovery from ECDSA nonce reuse
ethereum:2021-07-10:anyswap-v3-router-mp.reason: The Anyswap V3 loss came from the attacker recovering the router's MPC private key, not from any contract flaw. Two transactions signed by the V3 MPC account reused the same ECDSA nonce (identical r value), which makes the secret key recoverable by elementary algebra; the signing stack is Anyswap's off-chain Go MPC node, and the router's Solidity simply honours calls from `mpc()`. The onchain response confirms the diagnosis: on the Ethereum AnyswapV4Router 0x6b7a87899490ece95443e979ca9485cbe7e71522 the MPC was rotated away from 0x8b44a687224496276811555efa3f2d0acd667a72 the day after the incident, in transaction 0x65651a6ba929fcb12ddcacd9a92fc131e1893dd0d0787f3c7cc787e4dad91ec6 (changeMPC(address), block 12806663, 2021-07-11T14:56:16Z, sent by the compromised MPC itself), with storage slot 0 (_oldMPC) becoming 0x8b44a687... and slot 1 (_newMPC) becoming 0x2a038e100f8b85df21e4d44121bdbfe0c288a869; nothing about the deployed code changed. This incident is distinct from the January 2022 AnyswapV4Router permit flaw already admitted as incidents/1/0xe50ed602bd916fc304d53c4fed236698b71691a95774ff0aeeb74b699c6227f7.json, which is a genuine code defect. Compromised credentials are excluded by METHODOLOGY, and a nonce-reuse bug in an off-chain signer is not executed EVM code.

ethereum:2021-08-28:bilaxy-erc-20-hot-wa.reason: Bilaxy's own announcement (2021-08-29) says its ERC-20 hot wallet was hacked and about 295 tokens transferred to 0xa14d5da3c6bf2d9304fe6d4bc6942395b4de048b. ethereum:2021-12-04:bitmart-hot-wallet-d.name: BitMart hot wallet drain
ethereum:2021-12-04:bitmart-hot-wallet-d.reason: BitMart's Ethereum and BNB Chain hot wallets are externally owned accounts and the theft is a long run of ordinary ERC20 and BEP20 transfer calls. eth_getCode for the BitMart hot wallet 0x68b22215ff74e3606bd5e6c1de8c2d68180c85f7 at block 13742126, the block before the first drain, is 0x (it carries an EIP-7702 delegation designator today, which post-dates the incident by years), and the collector 0x39fb0dcd13945b835d47410ae0de7181d3edf270 is likewise an EOA. ethereum:2022-01-17:crypto-com-2fa-bypas.name: Crypto.com 2FA bypass withdrawals
ethereum:2022-01-17:crypto-com-2fa-bypas.reason: The loss came from Crypto.com's own withdrawal system approving unauthorised requests, not from any contract. The onchain fingerprint is unambiguous: the collector 0x6e1218c55f1acb588fc5e55b721f1183d7d29d3d has code 0x and received 282 inbound value transfers from 282 distinct sender addresses totalling 4,836.25962449635 ETH, all inside two hours on 2022-01-17 between block 14024742 at 18:44:35Z (first transaction 0x49121cabf0b68f4755aa766090cbbc4fde4cca79d62365dadc4c92a83c683cda, 8.4207791732 ETH from 0x0c405c16c379b67d256f6883803e68d50dd2f327) and block 14025319 at 20:55:35Z. ethereum:2023-04-09:gdac-exchange-hot-wa.reason: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Hot Wallet Key Compromised', targetType 'CEX', 13.9m USD, with no chain attribution at all because the drained assets were custodial balances rather than protocol positions: about 61 BTC, 350.5 ETH, 10,000,000 WEMIX and 220,000 USDT, roughly a quarter of the Korean exchange GDAC's total custody. ethereum:2023-04-14:bitrue-hot-wallet-dr.reason: Bitrue's own statement of 2023-04-14 reports 'a brief exploit in one of our hot wallets on 07:18 (UTC)' and about 23m USD withdrawn in ETH, QNT, GALA, SHIB, HOT and MATIC from a custodial wallet holding under 5 percent of exchange funds; SlowMist Hacked and DefiLlama both record it as a hot-wallet key compromise. ethereum:2023-06-02:atomic-wallet-client.name: Atomic Wallet client key exfiltration
ethereum:2023-06-02:atomic-wallet-client.reason: The victims are individual users' externally owned accounts across roughly 13 chains (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, BSC, Polkadot, Avalanche, XRP and others) and the keys were obtained off-chain from the Atomic Wallet client or its distribution/update path. A representative Ethereum leg is block 17395844 index 5, 2023-06-02T21:56:23Z, transaction 0x9d6903b106a948d20f6b967a6fa1c2472b73868e00ca2496fc7c1f37d4cc1d86: 304.363031583184322615 ETH with empty calldata from user EOA 0xb02dab4490fec2deaecc336f8b8b5e10dd8c6072 to drainer 0x391628df29ac2b66c11ae9515289a26be06a6340, which has code 0x and exactly one inbound value transfer - one of many single-use collectors. ethereum:2023-07-22:coinspaid-infrastruc.name: CoinsPaid infrastructure compromise
ethereum:2023-07-22:coinspaid-infrastruc.reason: CoinsPaid's own post-mortem states that the attackers did not obtain hot wallet private keys but instead gained access that allowed them to create authorised withdrawal requests, which CoinsPaid's own system then perceived as valid and forwarded to the blockchain. The theft and laundering path covers Ethereum and Avalanche C-Chain alongside non-eip155 Bitcoin and Tron, but every movement is an ordinary transfer authorised by CoinsPaid's own custody system, so no contract was exploited and no executed EVM code failed an invariant. Neither CoinsPaid, Match Systems, Elliptic nor the press coverage publishes victim wallet addresses or transaction hashes, so no candidate victim can be named; even with them, an offchain authorisation failure yields no code-age observation. Not to be confused with the separate 2024-01-06 CoinsPaid hot wallet incident of about 7.5m USD.

ethereum:2024-02-14:duelbits-casino-hot-.name: Duelbits casino hot wallet drain
ethereum:2024-02-14:duelbits-casino-hot-.reason: Web3 Is Going Great (https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/?id=duelbits-hack), citing PeckShield and Scam Sniffer, reports about 4.6m USD moved out of the crypto casino's custodial hot wallets on Ethereum, BNB Chain and Tron by ordinary signed transfers, attributed to a compromised private key; the site's own contracts are not in the path. A custodial EOA drain has no victim contract and no code age.

ethereum:2024-02-16:fixedfloat-custodial.name: FixedFloat custodial wallet drain (first 2024 incident)
ethereum:2024-02-16:fixedfloat-custodial.reason: FixedFloat is a custodial instant-exchange service, not a protocol. About 26.1m USD of Bitcoin and Ethereum was taken from its own service wallets; FixedFloat confirmed the theft on 2024-02-18 and, as with its 2024-03-31 repeat, attributed the entry to vulnerabilities in third-party services it depended on rather than to anything it had deployed onchain. Both SlowMist Hacked and DefiLlama classify the event as third-party/infrastructure key leakage. The movement of funds is EOA-to-EOA on the Ethereum leg and UTXO spends on the Bitcoin leg; no smart contract of FixedFloat's was executed, so there is no victim contract to name and no executed EVM code whose age could be measured. I could not obtain a spot-checkable attacker address for this incident from any primary source, and the exclusion does not depend on one: a custodial service compromised through its own infrastructure is outside the cohort whatever the addresses are.

ethereum:2024-02-27:serenity-shield-sers.name: Serenity Shield SERSH MetaMask wallet key leak
ethereum:2024-02-27:serenity-shield-sers.reason: Cointelegraph (https://www.tradingview.com/news/cointelegraph:244a74751094b:0-serenity-shield-s-token-falls-nearly-99-after-metamask-wallet-breach/) and crypto.news (https://crypto.news/serenity-shield-token-collapses-by-95-after-5-6m-breach/) report that at 09:11 UTC on 2024-02-27 6.9m SERSH (nominally 5.6m USD, sold for about 586k USD) was transferred out of one of the project's MetaMask EOAs after its private key leaked. An ordinary token transfer signed with a stolen key yields no victim contract.

ethereum:2024-03-17:remilia-treasury-pas.name: Remilia treasury password-manager compromise
ethereum:2024-03-17:remilia-treasury-pas.reason: The Block (https://www.theblock.co/post/282972/remilia-founder-charlotte-fang-claims-he-was-hacked-as-treasury-is-drained-of-millions) and Unchained (https://unchainedcrypto.com/milady-founder-claims-hack-after-millions-in-eth-and-nfts-drained/) report that the Remilia treasury multisig's signer keys were all stored in one Bitwarden vault that the founder says malware compromised; about 490 ETH, 58k USDC and hundreds of Milady, Remilio and NFTX assets (about 6m USD at floor) were moved by transactions the stolen keys signed. Some observers suspected an inside job; either way no contract check was bypassed.

ethereum:2024-03-21:airdao-amb-eth-unisw.name: AirDAO AMB/ETH Uniswap liquidity key theft
ethereum:2024-03-21:airdao-amb-eth-unisw.reason: AirDAO's disclosure reported by ForkLog (https://forklog.com/en/airdao-suffers-1-million-platform-breach/) and crypto.news (https://crypto.news/airdao-suffers-exploit-hackers-transfer-stolen-funds-to-mexc-kucoin-changenow/) says an attacker gained access through a phishing email with a malicious attachment impersonating a partner and removed the project-owned AMB/ETH Uniswap liquidity, 126.5 ETH and 41.61m AMB (about 1m USD). The Uniswap position was withdrawn by its owner's stolen credentials; Uniswap behaved as designed.

ethereum:2024-04-01:fixedfloat-second-cu.name: FixedFloat second custodial drain via third-party service
ethereum:2024-04-01:fixedfloat-second-cu.reason: CoinDesk (https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2024/04/02/bitcoin-lightning-exchange-fixedfloat-sees-suspicious-transfers-of-3m-to-ethereum-tron) and Web3 Is Going Great (https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/?id=fixedfloat-hack-2) report that on 2024-04-01 about 3m USD of ETH, USDT, WETH, DAI and USDC left the custodial instant exchange's wallets to Ethereum and Tron addresses, which FixedFloat attributed to a vulnerability in a third-party service, by the same group as its February breach. Custodial wallets were emptied through compromised offchain access; no victim contract exists.

ethereum:2024-06-04:lykke-exchange-custo.name: Lykke exchange custodial wallet drain
ethereum:2024-06-04:lykke-exchange-custo.reason: The Swiss exchange Lykke lost about 22.4m USD, roughly 158 BTC and 2,161 ETH plus other assets, on 2024-06-04; the 2024-06-09 candidate date is the date the theft was publicised, not the date it happened. The published sinks are Bitcoin bc1qt64756h9aylujm9tpk826zndegpxtngmr6eqad and Ethereum 0x9172a72f5009ca609833819763a2722e53806443. Spot check: 0x9172a72f5009ca609833819763a2722e53806443 is an externally owned account (code size 0) and its earliest inbound transactions are plain ETH value transfers on 2024-06-04, 189.0165 ETH at 06:48:11Z from 0xc43d1cbacba9dda683a6286a95673c722c0fc488, 1,385.8617 ETH at 06:50:11Z from 0x054e993e0ecc5bf2797515adfc81d58cb8de0478, 300.0141 ETH at 08:05:23Z from 0x1bb2e2d4c782e0a0ea4341f20efdd93b730b1119 and 318.9896 ETH at 08:39:23Z, i.e. several Lykke custodial EOAs emptied in sequence. No contract was called, so no executed EVM code failed and there is no victim contract.

ethereum:2024-06-09:loopring-official-gu.name: Loopring Official Guardian 2FA service compromise
ethereum:2024-06-09:loopring-official-gu.reason: Loopring's post-mortem (https://medium.com/loopring-protocol/postmortem-incident-report-and-path-forward-aa64f7e5f7d1) and The Block (https://www.theblock.co/post/299177/loopring-suffers-5-million-hack-after-guardian-two-factor-authentication-service-is-compromised) show the attacker compromised Loopring's offchain 2FA service, used it to obtain Official Guardian approval for wallet-recovery requests on smart wallets whose only guardian was the Official Guardian, reset ownership and withdrew about 5m USD. The wallet contracts correctly honored guardian-approved recovery; the failure was the offchain authentication service.

ethereum:2024-06-22:coinstats-hosted-wal.name: CoinStats hosted-wallet AWS breach
ethereum:2024-06-22:coinstats-hosted-wal.reason: CoinStats' incident report covered by DL News (https://www.dlnews.com/articles/people-culture/coinstats-issues-security-incident-report-on-june-attack/) and BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/cryptocurrency/coinstats-says-north-korean-hackers-breached-1-590-crypto-wallets/) says a socially engineered employee installed malware that gave suspected Lazarus actors access to CoinStats' AWS infrastructure, from which keys of 1,590 app-hosted wallets were used to drain about 2.2m USD. The victims are EOAs whose keys CoinStats held offchain.

ethereum:2024-08-07:nexera-nxra-proxy-ow.name: Nexera NXRA proxy-owner credential compromise
ethereum:2024-08-07:nexera-nxra-proxy-ow.reason: Nexera's post-mortem (https://nexera.medium.com/240807-incident-post-mortem-report-5f1f7840d4d7) and CoinDesk (https://www.coindesk.com/business/2024/08/07/blockchain-protocol-nexara-suffers-18m-exploit-nxra-tumbles-40) state that malicious code on a team machine exposed the credentials managing the Fundrs contracts; the attacker took ownership of the NXRA proxy, upgraded it and used the admin withdraw function to take 47.24m NXRA, of which 14.75m (about 449k USD; about 1.8m USD nominal) was sold. Ownership and admin withdrawal behaved as designed for the stolen credentials.

ethereum:2024-09-11:indodax-withdrawal-s.name: Indodax withdrawal system compromise
ethereum:2024-09-11:indodax-withdrawal-s.reason: SlowMist's analysis of the Indodax incident explicitly rules out a hot-wallet key compromise and concludes the exchange's withdrawal system itself was hacked, the attacker issuing round-number withdrawals (1 BTC, 3 BTC) with change returned to Indodax-controlled addresses; DefiLlama records the same event as infrastructure key leakage across Ethereum, Polygon and Optimism as well as Bitcoin, for 20-22m USD. Every leg is a custodial exchange wallet, an externally owned account acting on instructions from a compromised offchain withdrawal pipeline. No deployed contract executed defective code, so there is no victim contract and no code-age observation; the exclusion is on offchain infrastructure, which the cohort excludes regardless of chain.

ethereum:2024-09-19:banana-gun-telegram-.name: Banana Gun Telegram message-oracle transfers
ethereum:2024-09-19:banana-gun-telegram-.reason: Banana Gun's disclosure reported by Cointelegraph (https://cointelegraph.com/news/banana-gun-crypto-bot-refunds-3m) and QuillAudits' analysis (https://www.quillaudits.com/blog/hack-analysis/banana-gun-exploit) show attackers abused a vulnerability in the bot's offchain Telegram message oracle to trigger manual transfers of about 3m USD in ETH out of 11 users' bot-custodied wallets, on both the EVM and Solana bots, which share only that oracle. The victim wallets are EOAs whose keys the bot's backend held; no deployed contract failed.

ethereum:2024-09-25:truflation-treasury-.name: Truflation treasury multisig malware key theft
ethereum:2024-09-25:truflation-treasury-.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-truflation-hack-september-2024) and Cointelegraph (https://cointelegraph.com/news/truflation-loses-estimated-5-million-malware-attack) report that malware, believed installed around Token2049, gave the attacker the private keys controlling Truflation's treasury multisig and personal wallets, from which about 5.23m USD on Ethereum and about 100k USD on seven other chains were transferred; customer and staking funds were untouched. The multisig accepted valid signatures from the stolen keys.

ethereum:2024-10-31:m2-exchange-hot-wall.name: M2 exchange hot wallet drain
ethereum:2024-10-31:m2-exchange-hot-wall.reason: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Hot Wallet Key Compromised', targetType 'CEX', 13.7m USD taken from the Abu Dhabi exchange M2 across Ethereum, Solana and Bitcoin. Two of the three legs (Solana, Bitcoin) are outside eip155, and the Ethereum leg is ERC-20 and ether transfers signed out of custodial externally owned accounts. M2 operates no deployed protocol contract on any chain, so there is no victim contract, no exploit transaction against deployed code, and no code state whose age could be measured. M2 covered the loss from its own reserves the same week; that does not create a contract-level defect.

ethereum:2024-11-03:metawin-frictionless.name: MetaWin frictionless-withdrawal hot wallet drain
ethereum:2024-11-03:metawin-frictionless.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-metawin-hack-november-2024) and Web3 Is Going Great (https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/single/metawin-casino-hack) report that on 2024-11-03 the attacker abused a flaw in the casino's backend 'frictionless withdrawal system', per CEO Richard Skelhorn, to have MetaWin's Ethereum and Solana hot wallets pay out about 4m USD, which went to KuCoin and roughly 115 linked addresses. The payouts were ordinary transfers from custodial EOAs authorized by the offchain withdrawal service; no deployed contract failed.

ethereum:2024-11-08:coinpoker-hot-wallet.name: CoinPoker hot wallet drain
ethereum:2024-11-08:coinpoker-hot-wallet.reason: Web3 Is Going Great (https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/?id=coinpoker-hack) and Cyvers' analysis (https://cyvers.ai/coinpokers-hack-a-comprehensive-analysis-by-cyvers) report that on 2024-11-08 an attacker who compromised a CoinPoker-controlled hot wallet made 82 transfers of at most 25k USD each within 50 minutes across BNB Chain, Ethereum and Polygon, about 2m USD in total, laundered through Tornado Cash; custody provider Fireblocks attributed it to CoinPoker's own configuration and deposit processes. A custodial wallet drain has no victim contract.

ethereum:2024-12-02:debox-operational-wa.name: DeBox operational wallet key leak
ethereum:2024-12-02:debox-operational-wa.reason: DeBox's statement summarized in Nominis' December 2024 report (https://www.nominis.io/insights/crypto-security-incidents-december-2024) attributes the loss of 31.03 ETH and 4.88m BOX (about 275k USD) to a leaked private key of an operational wallet, unrelated to user funds, and commits to moving that account to a multisig. The assets left an EOA by transfers signed with the leaked key; no contract failed.

ethereum:2025-01-01:noones-hot-wallets-d.name: NoOnes hot wallets drained via internal Solana bridge
ethereum:2025-01-01:noones-hot-wallets-d.reason: The Block (https://www.theblock.co/post/337004/noones-ceo-ray-youssef-8-million-exploit-crypto-sleuth-zachxbt-investigation) and Merkle Science (https://www.merklescience.com/blog/hack-track-noones-flow-of-funds-analysis) report that on 2025-01-01 hundreds of sub-7,000 USD withdrawals emptied about 7.9m USD from the custodial P2P marketplace's hot wallets on Ethereum, Tron, Solana and BNB Chain; CEO Ray Youssef attributed it to a flaw in the platform's own Solana bridge integration, since disabled. The EVM legs are ordinary transfers from custodial EOAs, and the named flaw is in the platform's Solana-side withdrawal machinery.

ethereum:2025-01-21:adspower-wallet-exte.name: AdsPower wallet-extension supply-chain injection
ethereum:2025-01-21:adspower-wallet-exte.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-adspower-hack-january-2025) and Risky Business (https://risky.biz/risky-bulletin-supply-chain-attack-at-adspower-browser-platform/) report that between 2025-01-21 and 2025-01-24 10:00 UTC attackers who compromised the AdsPower antidetect browser injected code into wallet extensions installed through it (MetaMask, Phantom and others) that exfiltrated seed phrases and private keys, then drained about 4.7m USD from users' wallets. The victims are EOAs emptied with stolen keys.

ethereum:2025-04-01:zapper-frontend-dns-.name: Zapper frontend DNS hijack and drainer approvals
ethereum:2025-04-01:zapper-frontend-dns-.reason: Zapper's domain was hijacked at the DNS layer and visitors were served a wallet-drainer page that asked them to sign ordinary ERC-20 approvals and Permit2 signatures; the subsequent transferFrom calls executed exactly as the token contracts specify. DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'DNS Hijack', chains 'Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Base', dated 2025-04-01, and notably records amount null - the 7.9m figure in the lead is an unsourced press estimate with no per-victim accounting. The victims are individual externally owned accounts, Zapper's own deployed contracts were not implicated, and no EVM code failed an invariant, so the incident yields neither a victim contract nor a measurable code state.

ethereum:2025-04-16:r0ar-staking-contrac.name: R0AR staking contractor storage backdoor
ethereum:2025-04-16:r0ar-staking-contrac.reason: R0AR's statement (https://www.theblock.co/press-releases/351357/1r0r-contract-exploited-by-external-developer-r0ar-responds-with-buyback-program) and SlowMist's April report (https://slowmist.medium.com/slowmist-monthly-security-report-april-estimated-losses-at-26-4-million-0f64e8a9f904) show a trusted external contractor deployed R0ARStaking with deployment-time storage writes inflating user.amount for his own address, then called the emergency withdrawal to take about 780k USD of ETH through Tornado Cash. The failing code was an author-planted backdoor, not a defect an outside caller could exercise.

ethereum:2025-05-08:bitopro-exchange-hot.name: BitoPro exchange hot wallet drain
ethereum:2025-05-08:bitopro-exchange-hot.reason: DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'Key Leaked via Infrastructure', targetType 'CEX', 11.5m USD, across Ethereum, Tron, Solana and Polygon. The Taiwanese exchange BitoPro's own disclosure and the subsequent DPRK attribution describe malware planted during a hot-wallet system migration that exfiltrated signing material from the exchange's own servers; the outbound movements are then ordinary transfers from custodial externally owned accounts. Two of the four legs (Tron, Solana) are outside eip155 and none of the four involves a BitoPro-deployed contract, so there is no victim contract and no defective executed code to age.

ethereum:2025-06-01:force-bridge-privile.name: Force Bridge privileged-key unlock drain
ethereum:2025-06-01:force-bridge-privile.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-force-bridge-hack-june-2025) and crypto.news (https://crypto.news/nervos-network-suffers-major-exploit-as-3-9m-in-crypto-is-stolen-from-force-bridge/) show that, after Magickbase announced the bridge's sunset, the attacker called the Force Bridge contracts' privileged unlock functions on Ethereum and BNB Chain with compromised operator keys, after about six hours of failed attempts, draining 60,400 DAI, 539 ETH, 898,300 USDC, 257,800 USDT and 0.79 WBTC (about 3.7m USD) to Tornado Cash. The access checks passed for the stolen keys; the lead's supply-chain account concerns how those keys leaked, not deployed code.

ethereum:2025-06-21:hacken-hai-bridge-mi.name: Hacken HAI bridge minter key leak
ethereum:2025-06-21:hacken-hai-bridge-mi.reason: Hacken's statements reported by The Block (https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2025-06-22-hacken-cites-human-error-after-private-key-leak-triggers-5-million-crash-in-hai-value-359097) and Rekt (https://rekt.news/hacken-rekt) say a private key holding minting privileges on the HAI bridge contracts was exposed by human error during bridge architecture changes; the attacker minted about 900m HAI on Ethereum and BNB Chain and dumped it for about 250k USD, and the uncompromised deployer then revoked the minter. The mint executed through a legitimately authorized minter.

ethereum:2025-07-15:bigone-production-ne.name: BigONE production-network supply chain compromise
ethereum:2025-07-15:bigone-production-ne.reason: SlowMist's incident alert states that BigONE's production network was breached and the operating logic of the account-management and risk-control servers was modified so that unauthorised withdrawals were signed and broadcast normally, and that no private keys were leaked. The named Ethereum sink is 0x9bf7a4ddca405929dba1fbb136f764f5892a8a7a; onchain it is an externally owned account (code size 0) whose earliest inbound transfers begin 2025-07-15T17:25:59Z and come from BigONE hot-wallet EOA 0xd4dcd2459bb78d7a645aa7e196857d421b10d93f (also code size 0): USDT 1,395,000 (tx 0x605e999e7be320c893...), INVI 4,702,000, XIN 20,730, CDT 1,901,300 and UNI 25,487 in the following minutes. The same actor holds BSC 0x9bf7a4ddca405929dba1fbb136f764f5892a8a7a, Solana HSr1FNv266zCnVtUdZhfYrhgWx1a4LNEpMPDymQzPg4R, Bitcoin bc1qwxm53zya6cuflxhcxy84t4c4wrmgrwqzd07jxm and Tron TKKGH8bwmEEvyp3QkzDCbK61EwCHXdo17c. Every EVM leg is a plain ERC-20 transfer between two EOAs: there is no victim contract and no defective executed code, only compromised offchain infrastructure.

ethereum:2025-07-24:woo-x-exchange-devel.name: WOO X exchange developer-environment phishing drain
ethereum:2025-07-24:woo-x-exchange-devel.reason: DefiLlama's hack registry (api.llama.fi/hacks) records this as classification 'Social Engineering', technique 'Phishing', targetType 'CEX', 14.0m USD, spread across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Arbitrum and BSC. The compromised asset was WOO X's own developer environment; the attacker then signed ordinary withdrawals out of exchange-custody wallets. One of the four asset legs (Bitcoin) is not an eip155 chain, and on the EVM legs an exchange hot wallet is an externally owned account: no contract of WOO X's executed, no protocol invariant was violated, and there is no deployed code whose age could be measured. WOO X published no contract address or exploit transaction and I could not obtain a spot-checkable custody address for any leg; the exclusion ground does not depend on one, because a phished developer credential is outside the cohort whichever address was drained.

ethereum:2025-09-12:shibarium-pos-bridge.name: Shibarium PoS bridge validator-key takeover
ethereum:2025-09-12:shibarium-pos-bridge.reason: The Shiba Inu team's security update (https://blog.shib.io/shibarium-bridge-security-update/) and CCN (https://www.ccn.com/education/crypto/shibarium-bridge-hack-shib-bone-crash-explained/) report that at 18:44 UTC on 2025-09-12 the attacker, holding compromised signing keys for 10 of 12 Shibarium validators plus 4.6m flash-borrowed BONE staked to reach two-thirds, signed a malicious checkpoint and pushed a fraudulent exit through the Ethereum PoS bridge, withdrawing 224.57 ETH, 92.6bn SHIB and other tokens (about 2.4m USD). The bridge accepted a validly signed supermajority checkpoint; the failure is key custody.

ethereum:2025-10-19:astra-nova-managed-a.name: Astra Nova managed-account key compromise
ethereum:2025-10-19:astra-nova-managed-a.reason: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Private Key Compromised', targetType 'AI Agent', 9.09m USD on Ethereum; the web lead agrees the compromised party was a third-party managed account rather than Astra Nova's own contracts. I checked the project's RVV token 0x80563fc2dd549bf36f82d3bf3b970bb5b08dbddb on BSC across blocks 65108334-65223513 (2025-10-19 to 2025-10-20): zero mints from the zero address and no single transfer at or above 10,000,000 RVV, so the token contract neither over-issued nor was drained and is not the victim. The loss is stolen-key movement of balances held in an externally owned or custodially managed account, with no deployed contract executing outside its specification and nothing whose code age could be measured.

ethereum:2025-10-30:garden-finance-solve.name: Garden Finance solver key leak
ethereum:2025-10-30:garden-finance-solve.reason: DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'Key Leaked via Infrastructure', 11.4m USD, across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base and Solana. Garden is an intent-based cross-chain swap protocol whose solvers hold their own inventory and sign fills; the compromise was of a solver's operational infrastructure, so the attacker moved solver-owned capital with a stolen key rather than defeating any invariant of Garden's HTLC contracts. The Solana leg is outside eip155. This is a different event from the 2026-07-26 Garden database breach (450k USD), which DefiLlama lists separately. No Garden contract was drained by an attacker without the solver's key, so there is no defect-bearing victim contract; if a later postmortem shows the settlement contracts released escrowed user funds on a signature they should have rejected, the lead should be reopened.

ethereum:2025-12-25:trust-wallet-browser.name: Trust Wallet browser extension 2.68 malicious release
ethereum:2025-12-25:trust-wallet-browser.reason: The loss originates in a poisoned build of the Trust Wallet browser extension (version 2.68), i.e. in JavaScript shipped to users' browsers, not in any deployed contract. DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'Supply Chain Attack', targetType 'Wallet', chains 'Ethereum, Bitcoin, Solana', language null, 8,500,000 USD, dated 2025-12-25. The drains are ordinary transfers and approvals signed with keys the extension handed to the attacker, spread across chains two of which (Bitcoin, Solana) are not eip155 at all; the ERC-20 contracts touched on the Ethereum leg behaved exactly as written. No deployed EVM code violated an invariant, so there is no victim contract and no code age to measure.

ethereum:2026-02-21:iotex-iotube-validat.name: IoTeX ioTube Validator owner-key malicious upgrade
ethereum:2026-02-21:iotex-iotube-validat.reason: IoTeX's incident review (https://blog.iotex.io/blog/how-iotex-responded-to-the-iotube-bridge-incident-a-full-month-in-review/) and Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-iotex-hack-february-2026) show an attacker who had compromised an employee's machine obtained the private key owning ioTube's Ethereum-side Validator contract and upgraded it to skip signature checks, gaining control of TokenSafe and MintPool; about 4.3-4.4m USD of USDC, USDT, IOTX, WBTC and BUSD was drained and 111m CIOTX and 9.3m CCS minted. The upgrade went through the owner key's legitimate authority.

ethereum:2026-04-14:cow-swap-cow-fi-doma.name: CoW Swap cow.fi domain hijack
ethereum:2026-04-14:cow-swap-cow-fi-doma.reason: CoW's post-mortem as reported by The Block (https://www.theblock.co/post/397432/cow-swap-pauses-protocol-amid-domain-hijacking) and The Cryptonomist (https://en.cryptonomist.ch/2026/04/17/cow-swap-domain-hijack/) says attackers used social engineering and forged identity documents against the .fi registry to take over the cow.fi DNS and serve a phishing interface at swap.cow.fi for several hours, costing users about 1.2m USD in malicious signatures; CoW Protocol's contracts and backend were not affected.

ethereum:2026-04-30:wasabi-protocol-depl.name: Wasabi Protocol deployer key via AWS heap dump
ethereum:2026-04-30:wasabi-protocol-depl.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-wasabi-protocol-hack-april-2026) and CoinDesk (https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/04/30/wasabi-protocol-drained-for-usd4-5-million-in-apparent-admin-key-compromise) show the attacker pulled the wasabideployer.eth private key from an exposed Spring Boot Actuator heap dump on Wasabi's AWS infrastructure and, with no multisig or timelock, appointed a malicious admin and upgraded contracts on Ethereum, Base, Berachain and Blast, taking about 5.7m USD. Admin and upgrade checks passed for the stolen key.

ethereum:2026-05-15:thorchain-asgard-vau.name: THORChain Asgard vault GG20 threshold-signature key reconstruction
ethereum:2026-05-15:thorchain-asgard-vau.reason: THORChain's published post-mortem attributes the 2026-05-15 loss of about 10.7m USD across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Base and BNB Chain to a vulnerability in the GG20 threshold-ECDSA implementation used by THORNode: a malicious node operator progressively leaked key material until it could reconstruct the complete private key of one Asgard vault. That signing stack is off-chain Go code, and DefiLlama's registry records language null and targetType 'Chain' for this row (contrast the two 2021 THORChain rows, which it labels Solidity). Once the vault key was held, the Ethereum-side Router 0xd37bbe5744d730a1d98d8dc97c42f0ca46ad7146 simply honoured transferOut calls from the vault address as its source specifies; an onchain review of every Router transaction in blocks 25096819-25111182 (2026-05-15T00:00Z to 2026-05-17T00:00Z) shows only routine transferOut and depositWithExpiry traffic from Asgard vault accounts, with no anomalous entry point, no upgrade and no failed authorisation check. A cryptographic flaw in an off-chain MPC library is not a defect in executed EVM code, and two of the four affected chains (Bitcoin, and THORChain's own Cosmos-SDK L1) are not eip155 at all.

ethereum:2026-05-24:stablr-1-of-3-mintin.name: StablR 1-of-3 minting Safe takeover

ethereum:2026-06-22:aztec-escape-hatch-u.name: Aztec escape-hatch unconstrained proof_id (whitehat fork reproduction)

On Polygon the same EOA takes 436,014.6 and 447,086.07 EASY from 0xf4ee731c6ebeae783f7a03ec5bfc18489c8a4db9 and 0x50735f9087a148f4ba4a0f0052511c3bc5687d4c, then the treasury EOA 0x6324b1f720a07435269ae84285b1bafa4800fb3e (also code 0x) yields 1,979,435.98 DAI, 2,050,166.555442 USDC.e, 1,854,474.025921 USDT and 139.2994785 WETH between 11:05:29Z and 11:07:11Z. solana:2022-02-02:wormhole-token-bridge-.name: Wormhole token bridge forged VAA
solana:2022-02-02:wormhole-token-bridge-.reason: The defect is in Wormhole's Solana core-bridge program, written in Rust, not in any eip155 contract. verify_signatures used the deprecated solana_program::sysvar::instructions::load_current_index, which reads the supplied account without checking that it is the real Instructions sysvar; the attacker passed a fabricated account that made the secp256k1 precompile check appear satisfied, posted a VAA with no valid guardian signatures, and called complete_wrapped to mint 120,000 whETH on Solana. The Ethereum side then behaved exactly as designed: the guardians observed the (fraudulent but on-chain) Solana burn and signed genuine VAAs, so the token bridge 0x3ee18b2214aff97000d974cf647e7c347e8fa585 released 93,750 ETH to 0x629e7da20197a5429d30da36e77d06cdf796b71a in three internal transfers - 10,000 ETH at 2022-02-02T18:26:03Z (0x4d5201dd4a377f20e61fb8f42e6f929ec16bcec918f0584e39241d15b254a80f), 3,750 ETH at 18:33:32Z (0xd31b155e259a403ebe69831fae0ec2b4bd33dfa090c43b605a57d5c72c4fbbc7) and 80,000 WETH at 18:28:37Z via completeTransferAndUnwrapETH, selector 0xc6878519, transaction 0x24c7d855a0a931561e412d809e2596c3fd861cc7385566fd1cb528f9e93e5f14, unwrapped at 18:48:48Z. Because the EVM contract's signature check passed on genuinely signed data, there is no defective EVM code to age.

solana:2022-03-23:cashio-cash-infinite-m.name: Cashio CASH infinite mint
solana:2022-03-23:cashio-cash-infinite-m.reason: Cashio was a Solana stablecoin protocol and the defective program is Rust running on the SVM, so it produces no eip155 code-age observation. The bug was a missing account-constraint chain in the mint instruction: the collateral bank account's `crate_collateral_tokens` was validated against the pool but the pool account itself was not validated against the crate, so an attacker could supply a fake Saber LP mint that chained back to attacker-controlled accounts and mint CASH against worthless collateral. Roughly two billion CASH were minted and drained for about 52.8m USD of UST/USDC LP collateral, and CASH depegged to zero. There is no EVM contract anywhere in the path - Cashio had no Ethereum, BSC or L2 deployment - so no victim contract, exploit transaction or executable code age can be recorded in this cohort. DefiLlama records the incident as Solana, 52.8m USD, missing input validation.
