stacks:2024-04-11:zest-protocol-clarity-.reason: Zest's security update (https://www.zestprotocol.com/blog/zest-protocol-security-update) and EXVUL's analysis (https://medium.com/@exvul/the-first-attack-on-bitcoin-defi-smart-contract-ec5e5976983e) show the attacker duplicated entries in the collateral list passed to Zest's lending contract so collateral was overvalued, borrowing out about 324,000 STX (about 1m USD) over five operations. Zest is a Clarity contract on Stacks, not an eip155 chain, so there is no EVM code to age.

stacks:2025-06-06:alex-protocol-self-lis.name: ALEX Protocol self-listing verification flaw
stacks:2025-06-06:alex-protocol-self-lis.reason: ALEX is a DEX/launchpad on Stacks and its contracts are written in Clarity, not Solidity, running on the Stacks (Clarity VM) chain. DefiLlama records chain 'Stacks', language 'Clarity', classification 'Access Control', technique 'Caller Impersonation', 8,373,000 USD, dated 2025-06-06; the self-listing path failed to verify that the caller matched the token being listed. Stacks is not an eip155 chain, has no EVM runtime and no code hash that the verifier could pin, so the incident yields no code-age observation for this dataset. ALEX's earlier 2024-05-16 loss (4.3m, phishing) is likewise out of scope.

starknet:2026-06-19:myswap-cl-fake-token.name: mySwap CL fake-token pool accounting drain
starknet:2026-06-19:myswap-cl-fake-token.reason: MySwap's security update (https://x.com/mySwapxyz/status/2067941891010711560) and Crypto Adventure (https://cryptoadventure.com/myswap-loses-305k-on-starknet-after-fake-evil-token-abuses-cl-pool-accounting/) report that at 07:15 UTC on 2026-06-19 an attacker used a fake EVIL token to corrupt mySwap CL pool accounting and drained about 137.96 ETH, 45,000 USDC, 19,900 USDT and 230,000 STRK (about 300k USD). mySwap is a Cairo contract on Starknet, outside eip155.

starknet:2026-09-17:nostra-money-market-.name: Nostra Money Market spot price manipulation
starknet:2026-09-17:nostra-money-market-.reason: DefiLlama records a $3.5m spot price manipulation on Starknet, which runs Cairo, not EVM.

stellar:2026-02-22:blend-pools-v2-oracle.name: Blend Pools V2 oracle manipulation
stellar:2026-02-22:blend-pools-v2-oracle.reason: DefiLlama records Blend Pools V2 on Stellar, 10.97m USD, classification 'Oracle Manipulation', technique 'Spot Price Manipulation'. Blend is a Soroban lending protocol; its pools are Rust/WASM contracts addressed by Stellar strkeys (C... contract IDs), not eip155 addresses, so no address, runtime bytecode or codeHash exists that this dataset could measure. The cohort is eip155-only, so the incident is excluded on chain grounds whatever the mechanism. Re-enter only if the cohort is ever widened beyond eip155.

stellar:2026-08-25:cometdex-share-accoun.name: CometDEX share accounting
stellar:2026-08-25:cometdex-share-accoun.reason: DefiLlama records a $717k share-accounting loss on Stellar.

sui:2025-09-07:nemo-protocol-sui-oracle-.name: Nemo Protocol Sui oracle exploit
sui:2025-09-07:nemo-protocol-sui-oracle-.reason: The Block (https://www.theblock.co/post/369766/sui-nemo-protocol-exploit) and CoinDesk (https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/09/08/sui-based-yield-protocol-nemo-exploited-for-usd2-4m-in-usdc) report that the attacker manipulated a price oracle in Nemo's Sui yield-trading Move modules to extract about 2.4m USDC, later bridged via Arbitrum to Ethereum. The vulnerable code and depleted pools are on Sui, outside eip155; the EVM legs are laundering.

sui:2025-10-15:typus-finance-oracle-modu.name: Typus Finance oracle-module exploit
sui:2025-10-15:typus-finance-oracle-modu.reason: Typus Finance runs on Sui (Move); the oracle-module exploit and approximately $3.44m impact executed outside any EVM state. No EVM code defect and no EVM anchor exist to measure.

sui:2026-04-21:volo-vaults-operator-key-.name: Volo vaults operator key compromise
sui:2026-04-21:volo-vaults-operator-key-.reason: Rekt (https://rekt.news/volo-rekt) and Bitcoin.com News (https://news.bitcoin.com/volo-protocol-loses-3-5-million-in-sui-blockchain-exploit-blocks-wbtc-bridge-attempt/) report that on 2026-04-21 an attacker with a compromised Volo admin/operator key drained its WBTC, XAUm and USDC vaults on Sui of about 3.5m USD (about 2m later recovered); GoPlus and ExVul confirmed a privileged key breach rather than a contract flaw. The vaults are Sui Move objects outside eip155.

sui:2026-04-29:aftermath-perpetuals-nega.name: Aftermath Perpetuals negative builder-fee exploit
sui:2026-04-29:aftermath-perpetuals-nega.reason: The Crypto Times (https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/04/29/aftermath-finance-perps-on-sui-exploited-for-1-14m/) and a technical breakdown (https://dev.to/mehvetero/how-one-missing-assert-drained-114m-from-aftermath-finance-a-signed-integer-exploit-on-sui-1db3) show the attacker supplied a builder fee that read as negative under the perpetuals module's signed comparison, which settlement converted into collateral credit, withdrawing about 1.14m USDC in 11 transactions. The defect is in a Sui Move module outside eip155.

sui:2026-06-09:haedal-vault-cross-versio.name: Haedal Vault cross-version share-accounting flaw
sui:2026-06-09:haedal-vault-cross-versio.reason: SlowMist's incident log (https://hacked.slowmist.io/?c=Other) and Haedal's recovery statement reported by Bitget News (https://www.bitget.com/news/detail/12560605466093) show the attacker used deprecated deposit paths left by a 2025 upgrade to mint inflated LP shares in Haedal's Sui vaults and redeemed them through the new paths for about 915k USD of excess underlying; Haedal replaced the SUI-USDC, ETH-USDC, DEEP-SUI, WAL-SUI, CETUS-SUI and LBTC-SUI vaults and covered losses. The vaults are Sui Move modules outside eip155.

supra:2026-07-23:solido-cash-oracle-misa.name: Solido Cash oracle misassignment
supra:2026-07-23:solido-cash-oracle-misa.reason: Solido Cash runs on the Supra blockchain (Move modules, CDP vaults, CASH/SUPRA pools), not an eip155 chain; the two-wave oracle-misassignment mint of 809,051.55 unbacked CASH and the 293,705,544.97 SUPRA extraction executed outside any EVM state. No EVM code defect and no EVM anchor exist to measure.

terra-classic:2023-04-10:terraport-devel.name: Terraport developer-wallet liquidity drain
terra-classic:2023-04-10:terraport-devel.reason: Cointelegraph (https://cointelegraph.com/news/terra-defi-project-terraport-suffers-2m-hack-days-after-launch) and Unchained (https://unchainedcrypto.com/terra-classic-dex-loses-2-million-in-exploit-days-after-launch/) report that Terraport's developer wallet changed the code of three liquidity-provision contracts hours before the DEX's pools were emptied of about 15.1bn LUNC, 9.4m USTC and 9.1m TERRA (about 2m USD), and the TerraCVita validator later called it an insider job. The contracts are CosmWasm contracts on Terra Classic, outside eip155, and the change was privileged.

terra:2024-07-30:terra-ibc-hooks-reentra.name: Terra IBC hooks reentrancy drain
terra:2024-07-30:terra-ibc-hooks-reentra.reason: Range Security's analysis (https://www.range.org/blog/terra-ibc-hooks-exploit-analysis) and The Block (https://www.theblock.co/post/308440/attacker-exploits-ibc-hooks-vulnerability-to-steal-tokens-on-terra-blockchain) show the attacker exploited an ibc-go/IBC-hooks reentrancy, patched upstream in April 2024 but reintroduced by Terra's June upgrade to a custom ibc-go 7.3.1, to drain CosmWasm contracts of about 60m ASTRO, 3.5m USDC, 500k USDT and 2.7 BTC (about 6.4m USD) until validators halted the chain at height 11430400. The defect is in the Cosmos SDK chain software, outside eip155.

ton:2026-05-11:tac-bridge-ton-side-count.name: TAC bridge TON-side counterfeit jetton deposits
ton:2026-05-11:tac-bridge-ton-side-count.reason: TAC's post-mortem (https://tac.build/blog/post-mortem-report-tac-bridge) states that at about 02:20 UTC on 2026-05-11 the attacker deployed counterfeit TON jetton wallets whose deposit notifications the bridge accepted without checking the canonical jetton wallet code hash, so the TAC EVM side minted and released about 2.85m USD of USDT, BLUM and tsTON. The failed verification is in the TON-side bridge contracts and sequencing, outside eip155; the TAC EVM contracts honored messages the bridge attested.

ton:2026-10-16:affluent-unbacked-mint.name: Affluent unbacked mint
ton:2026-10-16:affluent-unbacked-mint.reason: DefiLlama records a $1.05m unbacked mint on TON.

tron:2024-06-23:sportsbet-io-hot-wallet-.name: Sportsbet.io hot wallet drain
tron:2024-06-23:sportsbet-io-hot-wallet-.reason: Web3 Is Going Great (https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/?id=sportsbetio-hack), citing ZachXBT, reports about 3.5m USD of USDT and TRX leaving the crypto sportsbook's custodial hot wallets by ordinary signed transfers, which the operator did not attribute to any contract. A custodial hot-wallet drain on Tron has no eip155 victim contract and no code age.

tron:2026-04-16:grinex-exchange-hot-wall.name: Grinex exchange hot wallet drain
tron:2026-04-16:grinex-exchange-hot-wall.reason: Grinex, the Kyrgyzstan-registered exchange that absorbed the sanctioned Garantex's liquidity and users, suspended trading and withdrawals after a hot-wallet infrastructure breach. Elliptic puts the theft at about 15m USD of USDT taken from Grinex-associated wallets and routed through TRON and Ethereum, then converted into TRX and ETH to reduce the chance of a Tether freeze; the exchange's own notice claims over 1bn rubles, about 13.1m USD. TRON is not an eip155 chain, and the Ethereum leg consists of ERC-20 transfers out of custodial externally owned accounts, so no deployed contract executed defective code and there is no victim contract to name.

tron:2026-05-11:transit-finance-legacy-t.name: Transit Finance legacy TRON router exploit
tron:2026-05-11:transit-finance-legacy-t.reason: Transit's announcement (https://x.com/TransitFinance/status/2054559075384590681) and Web3 Is Going Great (https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/?id=transit-finance-hack) report that an early-version Transit contract deployed on TRON and deprecated in 2022 was exploited through historical vulnerabilities for about 1.88m USD, later bridged into DAI on Ethereum; Transit said its current contracts were unaffected and compensated users. The vulnerable code runs on the TRON Virtual Machine, which is not an eip155 chain.

tron:2026-09-12:chainflip-amm-tron-bridg.name: Chainflip AMM Tron bridge flaw
tron:2026-09-12:chainflip-amm-tron-bridg.reason: DefiLlama records a $736k bridge logic flaw on Tron, not an eip155 chain.

venom:2026-07-26:chainconnect-venom-call.name: ChainConnect Venom callback-sender check
venom:2026-07-26:chainconnect-venom-call.reason: 0xposed's incident record (https://0xposed.io/radar/chainconnect-bridge-callback-exploit-white-hat-resolution) places the flaw in ProxyMultiVaultAlien_V10.onCheckAccumulatedFee on Venom 2.0, which failed to authenticate the callback sender, letting an unauthorized caller trigger releases of about 650k USD from the bridge's Ethereum, BNB Chain, Avalanche and Polygon vaults in 23 transactions; 280 ETH (82.9%) was returned on 2026-07-30 under a whitehat deal. The vulnerable code runs on Venom's TVM, outside eip155; the EVM vaults honored the bridge's attestations.

web:2024-10-25:aark-digital.name: Aark Digital
web:2024-10-25:aark-digital.reason: Aark's update (https://aarkdigital.medium.com/incident-of-october-25th-d074f32d6535), as quoted by the Quadriga case study (https://quadrigainitiative.com/casestudy/aarkdigitalincorrectbalanceupdateexploit.php), says a GMX callback failure during the GM delisting led Aark to run its own script converting users' GM to USDC, and that the script's incorrect balance update moved one user's USD value from 0.498942 to 498,942e12. Aark said the error was not in a deployed contract. Onchain, Aark's keeper 0x179ec6b252aaa2740da7535a59bc2cb6310a031a sent 48 transactions to 0x4213d42a5a6bd38ef9a166b179d1f360ff536d39 in blocks 266800000-267330000 (2024-10-23 to 2024-10-25), all of them withdrawal batches (0x9d5868e8); none updated a balance onchain. On 2024-10-23 the keeper submitted withdrawals of 498941999998.128 USDC signed by account 0x589197b4afc9e50a2cc872540a3760c624bbf97c, the inflated ledger balance, and they reverted (0x06bd68abdde6476ace84aa925164f0f4aaa538590a63f7f1c71f7b8e09dc9dc4). From 2024-10-24 23:39 UTC it paid out that account's smaller withdrawals from vault 0x7a5df878e195d09f1c0bbba702cfdf0ac9d0a835, among them 1,199,999.5 USDC in 0xac0464827a52d91b9be354665ad3758bded7aaf4e26415d25769f79f7326264f. The proceeds went to 0x58f87e302371550f7f525afd96086731d05dd582 and 0x64ad619e56611148a19bb8f89ec7251e0df791bd, two of the three exploiter wallets Aark named. Aark revised the loss to 1,499,841 USDC and 159.09 ETH. The vault paid out what Aark's offchain ledger and keeper authorised.

web:2024-12-01:clipper.name: Clipper
web:2024-12-01:clipper.reason: Clipper's Base pool ClipperPackedVerifiedExchange 0xb32d856cad3d2ef07c94867a800035e37241247c (verified) mints and burns pool tokens only for amounts its offchain signer approved: depositSingleAsset checks the transferred input and the signed poolTokens, and withdrawSingleAsset pays the signed assetAmount for the signed poolTokens. The attacker EOA 0xc39b43b22942be138d917447d1f41a6dd5fd1ff9 (contract 0x4bbcf14f on Base, 0x38ec13d7 on Optimism) paired validly signed quotes: in 0x5db01a68 the first pair deposited 5.4136 WETH for 21,360.69 pool tokens and withdrew the same pool tokens for 5.4506 WETH, about 0.7% more. That was repeated 50 times per transaction across 36 Base transactions on 2024-12-01 and 8 Optimism transactions. The onchain checks held. The mispricing is in the signing API's bundled swap-plus-withdrawal quotes, which Clipper itself named and disabled. Same pattern as the ApolloX and Zerogoki offchain exclusions.

wemix:2025-02-28:wemix-play-bridge-vault.name: WEMIX Play Bridge Vault monitoring-key withdrawals
wemix:2025-02-28:wemix-play-bridge-vault.reason: The WEMIX Foundation attributes the 8.65m WEMIX drain across 13 successful of 15 withdrawals to stolen authentication keys for the NILE NFT platform monitoring system, uploaded to a shared repository and held by the attacker for two months before use. No smart-contract vulnerability is evidenced; the vault released funds to correctly authenticated withdrawal requests.

wemix:2026-07-26:wemix-admin-privilege-m.name: WEMIX$ admin-privilege mint
wemix:2026-07-26:wemix-admin-privilege-m.reason: WEMIX discloses the attacker gained administrator privileges over the WEMIX$ contract and minted about 5,225,525 WEMIX$, swapping part into 30,736 WEMIX and 724,198.27 USDC.e before bridging out; about $724,000 was siphoned externally while the headline $6.25m counts the briefly circulating unauthorized issuance. The mint executed through the admin privilege as designed, with no evidenced defect in the deployed contract logic. The WEMIX3.0 chain is not an eip155 chain either, so both cohort conditions fail independently.

zksync:2023-04-26:merlin-dex-feeto-addre.name: Merlin DEX feeTo-address approval drain
zksync:2023-04-26:merlin-dex-feeto-addre.reason: Halborn's analysis (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-merlin-dex-hack-april-2023) and CoinDesk (https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2023/04/27/dex-merlin-and-certik-plan-to-compensate-2m-to-users-impacted-in-rugpull) show the feeTo address set at deployment held maximum token approvals from the pools, a centralization risk CertiK had flagged, and was used during the MAGE liquidity generation event to pull about 1.82m USD of USDC and ETH; Merlin and CertiK treated it as a rug pull by team members. The pools honored a privileged address the deployer configured; no permissionless defect is evidenced.

zksync:2023-07-28:kannagi-finance-vault-.name: Kannagi Finance vault rug pull
zksync:2023-07-28:kannagi-finance-vault-.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-kannagi-finance-rug-pull-july-2023) and crypto.news (https://crypto.news/zksync-eras-kannagi-finance-rug-pulls-and-steal-2-13m/) report that the Kannagi team emptied its zkSync Era vaults of about 2.13m USD, leaving 0.17 USD TVL, deleted its website, X and GitHub, and moved about 600 ETH through Tornado Cash; the live vault code was unverified and differed from the audited code. The loss is a team exit, not an exploit of a defect by an outside caller.

zksync:2024-06-07:gemholic-gemstoneido-t.name: Gemholic GemstoneIDO team withdrawal
zksync:2024-06-07:gemholic-gemstoneido-t.reason: Cointelegraph (https://cointelegraph.com/news/gemholic-scam-suspected-rug-pull-zksync) reports that 921 ETH of IDO proceeds, stuck in Gemholic's GemstoneIDO contract since April 2023 because of zkSync's transfer() gas behavior, became withdrawable after zkSync's v24 upgrade on 2024-06-07, and the team, which had promised refunds for a year, withdrew all of it (about 3.5m USD) to an unrelated wallet and deleted its accounts. The team took funds it controlled; no outside exploit occurred.

zksync:2025-04-15:zksync-airdrop-admin-k.name: ZKsync airdrop admin key sweepUnclaimed mint
zksync:2025-04-15:zksync-airdrop-admin-k.reason: Halborn (https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-zksync-hack-april-2025) and ZKsync's confirmation reported by blocmates (https://www.blocmates.com/news-posts/zksync-reports-5m-token-loss-from-compromised-airdrop-admin-account) show the private key of admin 0x842822c797049269A3c29464221995C56da5587D, which controlled three airdrop distributor contracts, was compromised and used to call the admin-only sweepUnclaimed() and mint about 111m unclaimed ZK (about 5m USD); 90% was later returned under a bounty. The admin function behaved as designed for its key holder.
